TK Kirkland joins VladTV for a blunt discussion on viral retail theft videos, from suspects running from security drones outside Ross to shoplifting incidents at Macy’s and in Las Vegas. Vlad then breaks down a shocking dollar store arrest where a woman accused of stealing allegedly refused handcuffs, claimed she was three months pregnant, grabbed an officer’s gun, and fired a shot in a residential street. According to the discussion, she later pleaded out and received a 40-year prison sentence after what began as a misdemeanor theft case escalated into serious felony charges.

Kirkland reacts to the decision-making, the role of the DA, and why he believes people should comply during arrests and fight their case later in court. The conversation touches on police encounters, resisting arrest, retail crime, viral videos, and the consequences of turning a minor shoplifting allegation into a life-changing criminal case.

--------
Royce White sits down with VladTV to revisit his turbulent freshman year at the University of Minnesota under coach Tubby Smith. The former top Minnesota basketball recruit explains why he stayed home despite offers from Kansas, Texas and other major programs, and reflects on the Mall of America petty theft case that led to his suspension.

White also details a separate campus laptop investigation, his no-contest plea context, and why he says University of Minnesota police later charged him with trespassing instead of theft. In a previously untold account, he discusses how tensions around Minneapolis and St. Paul friends visiting campus contributed to scrutiny from the athletic department. White addresses being blamed after a college football player was stabbed, saying the incident shaped his decision to transfer to Iowa State and influenced his later political views. A candid look at NCAA basketball, campus policing, race, reputation and accountability.

They discuss their 2022 guilty pleas to telecommunications fraud, probation and community service, plus the 2024 New York finding, $1.25 million settlement, and FCC fines exceeding $5 million. The pair defend the calls as political speech, citing vote-by-mail concerns, election integrity, and data brokers including LexisNexis, TLO, and Locate Plus.

The conversation also covers Detroit, Lansing, Pennsylvania, California, Virginia, MAGA politics, and claims about government use of voter data. Burkman and Wohl respond to Politico’s reporting on the AI lobbying firm LobbyMatic and alleged aliases “Jay Klein” and “Bill Sanders,” while revisiting past controversies involving Robert Mueller, Pete Buttigieg, Anthony Fauci, Brett Kavanaugh, Donald Trump, Joe Biden, and the 2024 election climate.

In this VladTV conversation, TS Madison reflects on her evolution from underground internet star and sex worker to mainstream media figure, while unpacking changing language around trans identity for cisgender viewers navigating respectful terms. Madison explains why she once used “transsexual,” how “transgender” became the broader term she learned through visibility from Laverne Cox, Carmen Carrera and other women in media, and why labels like “tranny” and “she-male” may not offend her personally but are hurtful and objectifying for many in the community. She also discusses “ladyboy” in the context of Thailand, Buddhist culture and social acceptance, contrasting it with America’s Christian-influenced attitudes. The interview traces her viral rise on social media and Vine, her influence on RuPaul’s Drag Race, World of Wonder, Logo TV and Viacom, plus her work with We TV’s The TS Madison Experience, Fox Soul, Drew Barrymore and Tosh.0.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Denvonta “Dirt Rocc” Lee revisits the events after Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson was jumped at the MGM Grand and the long-debated 1996 Las Vegas shooting of 2Pac. Dirt Rocc discusses Keefe D’s account, Club 662, Suge Knight, Death Row Records, and claims that guns were obtained before the group searched for Tupac. He also says his former roommate Big Dre personally told him, “that was me,” challenging the widely repeated claim that Orlando Anderson was the shooter.

Dirt Rocc explains why he believed Big Dre, describes Orlando’s shoulder injury, and rejects stories that Orlando bragged around Compton. He also talks about Terrence “Bubble Up” Brown, Freaky Dre, Knockout, and the tensions between Southside Compton Crips, Mob Piru associates, and rap-world politics surrounding Tupac Shakur’s death. A detailed look at one of hip-hop’s most debated cases.

--------
In this candid VladTV conversation, Nicholas Irving opens up about experiencing racism and harsh “hazing” during his time in the Army’s Third Ranger Battalion, including the disturbing moment someone placed a noose in his locker when he was a new sniper. Joined by Robert O’Neill, the discussion explores military culture, race, dark humor, and where the line gets crossed inside elite units.

Irving reflects on growing up in predominantly Black Baltimore before entering the military, where he encountered a very different environment and conversations around race. The interview also touches on his path toward becoming a Navy SEAL, how colorblindness affected his plans, training in Annapolis, and the unexpected turns that led him into the Rangers instead. O’Neill adds perspective from the SEAL community, with stories spanning BUD/S-style hardship, Newport, Rhode Island dive training, and memories involving Jocko.
